title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
supported_claims: DAS learns orthogonal alignments using supervised interchange interventions; demonstrations use hierarchical equality and natural-language inference.
limitations: The high-level variables and counterfactual answers are supplied; alignment is not unsupervised discovery of a generator.
voynich_implication: Retain low-rank causal alignment as synthetic calibration; demand new-key transition transfer before manuscript interpretation.

title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
supported_claims: Formalizes mechanism transformations and graded causal faithfulness across several intervention methods.
limitations: Abstract inspected here; the 64-page derivations were not audited. Formal faithfulness remains relative to the chosen abstraction and intervention family.
voynich_implication: Specify the proposed state variable, update rule and intervention correspondence before claiming a circuit.

title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking For? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
sections_read: arXiv v2 abstract for version comparison
supported_claims: Successful output changes can arise through dormant pathways, so steering and natural computation can diverge.
limitations: The definition and empirical interpretation are disputed by M04. The ICLR author list differs from the older arXiv record; do not merge versions silently.
voynich_implication: Keep output-span, shuffled-supervision, untrained-model and earlier multi-step controls together.

title: A Reply to Makelov et al. (2023)'s 'Interpretability Illusion' Arguments
supported_claims: Shows a proposed illusion diagnostic can reject an intuitive valid direction; multiple causal abstractions can coexist.
limitations: A rebuttal of one diagnostic does not make arbitrary steering faithful; task, alignment and intervention support still matter.
voynich_implication: Do not use nullspace removal alone as a universal veto. Test a whole intervention algebra and held-out transitions.

title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
supported_claims: Localization results depend on corruption and scoring choices.
limitations: Semantic replacement is controlled in their tasks; manuscript donors have no known semantic answer. Metric recommendations are task-dependent.
voynich_implication: Pre-register donor matching and report absolute KL/loss changes, not only normalized recovery.

title: Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
supported_claims: Cross-layer transcoders replace MLP computations with sparse features; attribution graphs expose prompt-specific dependencies.
limitations: The local attribution graph freezes attention, unlike the ordinary replacement forward pass; reconstruction, inhibition and substitute-mechanism faithfulness remain limitations. Frontier CLT training is expensive.
voynich_implication: Use a small frozen-model pilot only after predictive-state tests succeed; measure intervention mismatch and retain error nodes.

title: A Toy Model of Mechanistic (Un)Faithfulness
sections_read: Full note, including repeated-data toy and Jacobian matching
supported_claims: A sparse transcoder can memorize repeated points absent from the original absolute-value mechanism; Jacobian matching mitigates this toy failure.
limitations: Explicitly preliminary; matching gradients can itself be gamed and exact matching may preserve superposition artifacts.
voynich_implication: Our repeated tiny corpus makes this a direct warning: compare intervention responses, not just reconstruction loss.

title: Tracing Attention Computation Through Feature Interactions
supported_claims: Bilinear query-key feature interactions explain attention scores; head loadings connect those scores with graph edges.
limitations: Retrieved primary-source excerpts rather than every derivation; pre-softmax attribution does not alone establish complete causal computation.
voynich_implication: If tracing prefix-state updates, explicitly test attention routing as well as MLP features.

title: Sparse Crosscoders for Cross-Layer Features and Model Diffing
supported_claims: Shared sparse features can reconstruct several layers or models and reduce duplicate-feature descriptions.
limitations: Preliminary note; shared representations can have different downstream roles, and crosscoder graphs can differ from original mechanisms.
voynich_implication: Compare seeds with shared dictionaries as a descriptive aid, then independently test functional substitution.

title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
supported_claims: Seven metric families across over 200 SAEs show reconstruction proxies need not track practical usefulness.
limitations: Several metrics rely on English labels or automatic explanations unavailable for unknown text. No metric alone establishes a state-update mechanism.
voynich_implication: Use reconstruction, cross-seed stability, synthetic ground truth and causal transfer separately; no single SAE quality score.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis
supported_claims: Stitching and meta-SAEs challenge completeness and atomicity of SAE features.
limitations: Does not imply SAEs are useless or all decompositions equivalent; dictionary size changes the analytical grain.
voynich_implication: Never label an SAE neuron as a discovered historical character class without competing resolutions and controls.

title: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders
sections_read: 4 synthetic experiment table and stability metrics
supported_claims: Introduces signed codes, approximate restricted-isometry regularization and multistep encoding; gains differ by regime and metric, with strong synthetic improvements and mixed real-activation stability/reconstruction tradeoffs.
limitations: Run-to-run statistical identifiability differs from identifying a true generative concept. Distributional and dictionary assumptions are material. Real-activation reconstruction improvement can accompany worse dictionary cosine/IoU stability.
voynich_implication: Pilot only against ordinary TopK and PCA on known ground truth; measure codes and subspaces, not decoder cosine alone.

title: Unstable Features, Reproducible Subspaces: Understanding Seed Dependence in Sparse Autoencoders
supported_claims: Individual instability can coexist with reproducible low-rank subspaces; stable features carry greater measured functional effects in their settings.
limitations: Cosine thresholds and masking define the measurements; 96-seed GPT-2 and other tested models do not establish tiny-corpus behavior.
voynich_implication: Test feature matching, principal-angle subspace agreement and functional substitutions across our seeds; retain random-model controls.

title: Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry in their Residual Stream
supported_claims: Known HMM beliefs can be linearly read from trained transformer activations; RRXOR requires information across layers beyond immediate forecasts.
limitations: Readouts use oracle beliefs. This version does not establish blind generator identification or a faithful state-update circuit.
voynich_implication: Diagnose RRXOR across layers and joint futures, rather than equating failed final-layer clustering with absent information.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Interpret Randomly Initialized Transformers
supported_claims: Automatic feature explanations and common SAE quality measures can look similar on random and trained transformers.
limitations: Abstract-level here; this challenges the sufficiency of those metrics rather than every causal use of SAEs.
voynich_implication: Every automatic naming or saliency claim needs an equally processed untrained backbone and held-out behavioral test.

title: Natural Language Autoencoders Produce Unsupervised Explanations of LLM Activations
supported_claims: An activation verbalizer and reconstructor use a natural-language bottleneck and reconstruction-driven reinforcement learning.
limitations: Pretrained language-capable modules supply semantic structure. Activation reconstruction is not a guarantee that descriptions recover unknown plaintext.
voynich_implication: Defer as a Voynich decoder; at most use independently tested descriptions of known synthetic variables.

title: Characterizing interference weights in a tiny language model
supported_claims: Studies virtual-weight effects in a 2.9M-parameter one-layer transformer without normalization or biases.
limitations: A single final-checkpoint local Fisher metric is narrower than global mechanism recovery; architecture and corpus differ from ours.
voynich_implication: Consider virtual-weight perturbation as a small-model diagnostic, calibrated against actual held-out interventions.

title: Jacobian Sparse Autoencoders: Sparsify Computations, Not Just Activations
supported_claims: Paired input/output SAEs penalize the Jacobian's density in feature coordinates, targeting sparse computation rather than only sparse activations.
limitations: Sparse Jacobians need not imply sparse computational graphs; initial method addresses a single MLP, not complete temporal dynamics.
voynich_implication: A possible local comparator to transcoders, with finite interventions and random-model controls; do not mistake gradient sparsity for a recovered algorithm.

title: The Belief State Transformer
supported_claims: Forward-prefix/backward-suffix training and two prediction objectives improve tested planning tasks; an ideal conditional-prediction theorem yields a future-sufficient representation.
limitations: The theorem assumes exact conditionals over all supported prefixes/suffixes. It does not establish unique generator recovery, finite-data optimization success, or a minimal historical state.
voynich_implication: Useful objective ablation for parity/delayed-information controls; causal evaluation must hide the future and compare equal training information.

title: Extracting Automata from Recurrent Neural Networks Using Queries and Counterexamples
supported_claims: L-star learning uses a trained RNN acceptor as oracle and refines state partitions using concrete disagreements.
limitations: An approximate equivalence oracle can terminate without proving global equivalence; the teacher's behavior, not the historical generator, is extracted.
voynich_implication: Require counterexample-guided refinement and finite stop limits; use a probabilistic extension for next-token models rather than silently binarizing text.

title: Causal Scrubbing: a method for rigorously testing interpretability hypotheses
supported_claims: A proposed interpretation specifies activation replacements that should preserve behavior; recursive resampling tests those invariances.
limitations: Needs a concrete hypothesis and equivalence classes; the authors explicitly note that it cannot eliminate every incorrect hypothesis.
voynich_implication: After discovering candidate variables on synthetic development data, test nuisance-preserving resampling and irrelevant-path removal on fresh cases.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features
supported_claims: Changing SAE seed can change discovered feature sets substantially; effects vary with architecture and sparsity.
limitations: A particular reported overlap is not a universal instability rate. Seed dependence alone does not exclude stable subspaces or useful interventions.
voynich_implication: Use paired feature/code/subspace comparisons rather than one attractive dictionary; M13 refines this question.

title: Weight-sparse transformers have interpretable circuits
sections_read: 1 causal circuit validation and capability tradeoff
supported_claims: Constraining weights and activations enables smaller circuits on curated tasks; sparsity trades capability for interpretability. Optimization retains dense gradients and moments.
limitations: Mean-ablation necessity/sufficiency is task-conditional; sparse training remains inefficient. Sparse coordinates need not map to historical units.
voynich_implication: Candidate small de-novo synthetic comparator, matched by predictive quality and exposure; budget memory using dense optimizer state.

title: Cross-Layer Transcoders are incentivized to learn Unfaithful Circuits
supported_claims: Cross-layer reconstruction can skip intermediate computations in a known toy; preliminary real-model comparisons yield differing circuit accounts.
limitations: Original author report from a one-week sprint; one author is listed by pseudonym. The later OpenReview PDF was access-blocked, so its version is not claimed read.
voynich_implication: Compare per-layer and cross-layer replacements against actual intermediate interventions before interpreting sparse graphs.
